findings.description: The bucket is explicitly commented as public with no acl attribute set to private and no public access block restricting access, allowing unauthenticated/unauthorized users to read or write objects such as customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket (including a customer master file) are not encrypted at rest.

A customer master spreadsheet (likely containing sensitive customer data) is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing sensitive data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is set for this bucket holding financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for the operations bucket, so stored objects are not encrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for the data_science bucket, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
